description:
Space Society is a team of technology and science enthusiasts driven by curiosity, innovation, and a shared passion for space exploration.

We believe technology should do more than explore the universe, it should help us understand and protect our own planet.
summary:
In arid mountainous watersheds like the Peruvian Andes, dry riverbeds can transform into catastrophic flash floods (huaicos) and volcanic lahars within hours. During these extreme storm events, optical satellites (Sentinel-2, Landsat) fail completely due to dense cloud cover and darkness.
To bridge this emergency gap, Space Society developed NISAR Hydro-Lens, an automated radar intelligence system powered by NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) L-Band L2 GCOV science granules (24 cm wavelength). Standard radar algorithms fail in arid landscapes because smooth desert sands mimic water (-18 dB), while narrow Andean gorges cause official NASA OPERA DSWx pipelines to collapse. Our breakthrough dual-sign multi-scale top-hat engine extracts river morphology directly from radar geometry, isolating open-water specular reflection (-19.5 dB) from flooded vegetation double-bounce (+1.8 dB).
Tested across 118 river reaches in Southern Peru, the platform achieves over 62% spatial agreement with verified ground hydrology, couples river dynamics with INGEMMET volcanic lahar hazard corridors from Mount Misti, and simulates 12-day orbital repeat cycles to deliver actionable early warning telemetry to civil defense agencies.
details:
1. What does it do and how does it work?

NISAR Hydro-Lens is an operational satellite radar intelligence dashboard and processing pipeline designed to detect, track, and forecast flash floods and volcanic debris flows (lahars) across arid and mountainous basins in Southern Peru.

The system works through a 4-stage scientific architecture:

  • Raw Sensor Ingestion: Ingests native 20m L2 GCOV (Geocoded Covariance) HDF5 granules from the NASA-ISRO NISAR mission via NASA ASF Earthdata Cloud, extracting calibrated $\text{HH}$ and $\text{HV}$ gamma-naught ($\gamma^0$) radar backscatter.
  • Dual-Sign Top-Hat Extraction: Overcomes the "radar desert dilemma" (where smooth dry sands reflect microwaves away, falsely mimicking open water) and the "vegetation barrier" (dense riparian trees creating a bright double-bounce return). Our custom mathematical filter (processing/gcov_rivers.py) applies a 600m directional structuring element combined with morphological elongation ($\text{length} \ge 1,500\text{m}$, $\text{aspect ratio} \ge 3$) to segment true hydrological ribbons regardless of whether they appear dark (open water) or bright (canopy double-bounce).
  • NASA OPERA DSWx Audit & DEM Shadow Mitigation: Evaluates and resolves the bimodal thresholding collapse observed in NASA/JPL's official OPERA DSWx-SAR pipeline over narrow valleys, filtering radar shadows using local slope and HAND (Height Above Nearest Drainage) terrain masks.
  • Hydrological-Volcanic Coupling: Maps volcanic lahar drainage pathways from active volcanoes (Misti and Sabancaya) that remit pyroclastic flows directly into the urban Chili River canyon, triggering automated telemetry alerts.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • All-Weather, 24/7 Vision: Microwave L-Band (24 cm wavelength) penetrates torrential storm clouds, volcanic ash plumes, and darkness where optical instruments (Sentinel-2, Landsat) are blind.
  • Sub-Canopy Detection: Long L-Band wavelengths pierce agricultural canopies and riparian forests, detecting floodwaters hidden beneath tree tops via corner-reflector double-bounce.
  • No Heavy Infrastructure Required: Includes a lightweight Python/FastAPI microservice querying precalculated SQLite geospatial river reaches, accompanied by automated one-click Windows launchers (iniciar.bat / detener.bat) and cross-platform runners (run.py).
  • Fully Bilingual (EN | ES): Instant single-click language toggle between English (for international space agency coordination) and Spanish (for regional civil protection and local communities).

3. What is the intended impact?

By providing continuous monitoring across 118 critical river reaches (Camaná, Majes, Chili-Quilca, Ocoña, and Tambo), the platform serves as an early-warning telemetry system for Peru's National Civil Defense (INDECI) and Disaster Risk Management agencies (CENEPRED, INGEMMET, ANA). It protects more than 1.4 million residents in metropolitan Arequipa and safeguards vital agricultural valleys from devastating unannounced flash floods.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Languages & Frameworks: Python 3.10–3.13 (NumPy, SciPy, Rasterio, H5Py, FastAPI, Uvicorn, PyTest), JavaScript (ES6+, Leaflet.js, Node.js), HTML5, TailwindCSS.
  • Radar & Satellite Libraries: NASA ASF CMR API, NASA/JPL OPERA DSWx-SAR runtime environment, GDAL/OGR.
  • Data Storage: SQLite with spatial indices for ultra-fast vector telemetry delivery under low emergency bandwidth.
  • Testing & Verification: 26 automated PyTest unit tests and 9 Node.js topological geometry tests passing at 100%.

5. How is your project creative?

Rather than relying on static decibel thresholds that inevitably fail in arid and rugged Andean topography, our solution treats river detection as a geometric and spatial morphology problem. We bridge satellite radar polarimetry with volcanic disaster management, recognizing that in Arequipa, flood risk cannot be decoupled from the volcanic ash and pyroclastic debris channelized into urban drainage ravines (torrenteras).

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Orbital Repeat Mechanics: Designed around NISAR’s exact 12-day orbital repeat cycle, modeling crest evolution from $+0\text{d}$ to $+72\text{d}$.
  • Emergency Bandwidth Limits: Delivering raw multi-gigabyte HDF5 files to field teams in disaster zones is impossible; our microservice precalculates lightweight vector geometries with embedded backscatter telemetry for low-latency delivery.
  • Physical Validation: Ground-truthed against official Peruvian hydrological baselines, achieving 62.5% spatial agreementwithin a 120m buffer.
